function.name: search
function.description: Search the corpus with one or more queries simultaneously. The top matching documents (union across all queries) are added to your working directory; documents already there from earlier searches are kept (the working directory accumulates evidence across this session). Returns a per-query top-10 preview with file paths and short snippets, and the new total working-directory size. Pass multiple complementary queries in one call. Specific distinctive terms (rare phrases, proper nouns, distinctive number/date combinations) tend to give the best results. New searches also return each subquery's search_id, offset and next_offset. A page call accepts only an actual returned search_id and optional zero-based offset (default 0), without queries. Each page contains at most ten original document-opening snippets in the original document BM25 order, with the same 100-character previews as the first page. Paging does not retrieve, import or score documents. Later searches do not invalidate these document-search IDs; next_offset=null means this fixed record is exhausted. These IDs are separate from rerank result IDs.

search_id.description: Actual document-search ID returned by search. Use without queries.

offset.description: Zero-based document offset for search_id; default 0, at most ten documents per page.

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a bash command in the current working directory. Useful for searching with `rg`, `grep`, listing with `ls`, `find`, or reading with `cat`, `head`. Output is truncated; use focused patterns and flags like `-l` to keep results manageable.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a file by path with optional line offset and limit. Returns numbered lines. The default limit (2000) is usually sufficient to read most documents in one call — prefer that to small limits, since the first 50-100 lines of many documents are navigation/template chrome, not content.

file_path.description: Path relative to the working directory.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-indexed). Default 0.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read. Default 2000; prefer the default unless you have a specific reason to read only a slice.

function.name: rerank
function.description: Find relevant original-body passages for your explicit evidence goal. Choose query, imported file subset, BM25 candidate count, retained count and output size yourself. Omitted files means the whole accumulated pool; [] means an empty scope. Returns source paths and read/bash coordinates, without restricting bash/read. For paging, supply result_id instead of query/file_paths/bm25_candidates; top_k, offset and limit can change without rescoring. Scores are relevance rankings, not verification of facts.

query.description: Explicit fact or relationship to verify, including known entity names; required for a new ranking.

file_paths.description: Optional list of already imported relative source paths, such as files selected with bash; omitted or null means the accumulated pool.

bm25_candidates.description: M: number of scope-local BM25 passages sent to the neural reranker; default 1000, adjustable per call.

top_k.description: K: retain up to this many ranked passages; K <= M. Default min(100,M), or the first request's K on a result page.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the retained ranking; default 0.

limit.description: Number of complete passages to return on this page; default 10, adjustable per call.

result_id.description: Tool-returned current ranking ID for pagination; mutually exclusive with query/file_paths/bm25_candidates.
